subject: Anatomy
concept: Bone marrow is a vascular, soft tissue within the medullary spaces of bones that provides the principal site of hematopoiesis after birth.

content.definition: Bone marrow is the soft tissue occupying the cavities and medullary spaces of bones. It contains hematopoietic tissue, stromal/supporting cells, adipocytes, and a specialized vascular network.
content.explanation: Bone marrow is both an anatomical compartment and a functional hematopoietic organ. Its microenvironment supports hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, their differentiation into blood-cell lineages, and release of mature cells into the circulation.
content.mechanism: Hematopoietic stem cells self-renew and differentiate through progressively committed progenitor stages. Developing blood cells occupy hematopoietic niches associated with stromal cells and vasculature; mature cells enter the circulation through marrow vascular sinusoids.
content.structure: The marrow space is organized around trabecular bone, vascular sinusoids, and stromal networks. Major cellular components include hematopoietic cells, endothelial cells, stromal/reticular cells, adipocytes, and other supporting cells.
content.function: The major function of active red marrow is hematopoiesis: production of erythrocytes, leukocytes, and platelets. The marrow microenvironment also regulates stem-cell maintenance, proliferation, differentiation, and trafficking.
content.clinical_relevance: Bone marrow examination is central to evaluating many hematologic disorders because marrow architecture and cellular composition reflect blood-cell production and disease processes.
content.diagnosis: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy can directly assess marrow cellularity, hematopoietic lineages, architecture, and abnormal infiltrates when clinically indicated.
content.treatment: Bone marrow itself is not a treatment; marrow-directed therapies and transplantation are used in selected hematologic diseases.
high_yield: Red bone marrow is hematopoietically active.
Yellow bone marrow contains predominantly adipose tissue and can contain hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells.
Bone marrow hematopoiesis occurs in a specialized microenvironment containing vascular and stromal components.
Developing blood cells gain access to the circulation through marrow vascular sinusoids.
In adults, active red marrow is concentrated mainly in the axial skeleton, with variable residual red marrow in parts of the proximal long bones.

terminology.etymology: Marrow derives from Middle English marrow, referring to the soft material within bones.
terminology.notes: Do not confuse bone marrow with spinal cord; they are anatomically and functionally distinct.

terminology.etymology: From Greek haima (blood) and poiein (to make).
